title: entropy-baker: compressive sequence sampler + per-kernel tail normalizer
author: Esther Park
release_notes: Adds a new workload generator (entropy-baker) and a reporting stage that normalizes per-kernel tail metrics. No config changes required for existing workloads; opt-in via new harness flag.
description:
Motivation: We frequently see spiky tail amplification in multi-sequence runs where a small cohort of long sequences drives kernel saturation and masks improvement signals. entropy-baker introduces a compressive sampler that biases synthetic sessions toward informative tail events while still keeping overall sequence distributions realistic. Paired with a per-kernel tail normalizer, this helps make small performance deltas visible in CI and reduces noise in regression detection.

What this PR does: Adds a new workload generator: entropy-baker, which synthesizes session traces by (1) building a histogram of observed sequence prefixes from corpus traces, (2) sampling rarer long-prefix events with importance weights derived from prefix entropy, and (3) emitting interleaved batches that preserve short/long ratio targets. Introduces a reporting pipeline stage: kernel_tail_normalizer, which ingests flame/timeline histograms and applies a robust scaling per kernel to remove cohort-level tail skew before aggregating quantiles.

Key benefits: - Reduces false-positive regressions from tail-saturated kernels in small sample CI runs. - Amplifies signal from long-sequence microbenchmarks so that optimizer changes (e.g., KV cache pruning, attention kernel tweaks) show consistent delta. - Lightweight: sampler runs client-side in the benchmark harness and adds <6% overhead to runner time for typical datasets.

Usage: New harness flag --enable-entropy-baker; config supports target_long_ratio, entropy_weight, and seed. Normalizer is enabled in reporting by default for benchmark-lab CI jobs that set report.normalizer=auto.

Validation: - Microbench: ran on 8-node local cluster, 4 model variants; entropy-baker increases long-seq sample density by 9x while keeping mean tokens-per-request within 5% of baseline. - Regression sensitivity: introduced a controlled 2% slowpath delay in attention kernel; without normalizer the delta was obscured (p95 delta 0.8%), with normalizer the delta surfaces at p95=2.1% and p99=3.4%. - Stability: 30 end-to-end runs show standard deviation of p95 reduced from 1.9% to 1.1% with normalizer. Full numbers in the commit benchmark output.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for sampler weighting and seed determinism. - [x] Integration test in bench-harness that toggles long/short mixes. - [x] Reporting tests validate scaled histogram aggregation. - [x] CI workflow adds a smoke run to benchmark-lab nightly.

Commits summary: - 9c4f5b1: initial entropy-baker sampler implementation and unit tests - 2a7d6be: integrate sampler into bench-harness and add config bindings - f1b8c3e: kernel_tail_normalizer implementation + histogram serializer changes - a4d2b8f: add e2e integration and benchmark payloads - d21f5ea: test fixes, docstrings, and CI workflow updates

Files changed (high-level): - bench/harness/samplers/entropy_baker.py: new sampler module, weighting algorithms, unit tests - bench/harness/config.yaml: new sampler flags and defaults - bench/reports/normalizers/kernel_tail_normalizer.py: new reporting stage + docs - bench/reports/serializers/histogram_v2.proto: serializer extension to carry normalized buckets - ci/workflows/benchmark-nightly.yml: add nightly smoke job using entropy-baker - docs/bench/entropy-baker.md: usage + tuning guidance - tests/bench/test_entropy_baker.py: deterministic tests - tests/reports/test_kernel_tail_normalizer.py: normalization edge cases

Notes on design decisions: - We intentionally keep the sampler separate from the core request generator to allow opt-in through flags without perturbing existing stress runs. - Normalizer uses a robust median-based scale with outlier clipping to avoid over-correcting for genuine regressions. - Serializer was extended to keep a normalization metadata field so downstream dashboards can toggle views with/without normalization.

Limitations and future work: - Current importance weighting uses prefix-frequency entropy; future iterations could incorporate latency-weighted entropy to bias on cost-sensitive events. - Normalizer is tuned for GPU attention kernels; additional kernel categories (quantized matmul paths) may need per-backend params.

Related: BENCH-78 for regression sensitivity improvements, ENG-4012 for CI false-positive reduction.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach — the entropy-weighting is intuitive. Two requests: add an explicit seed propagation path so CI reproducibility isn't relying on global RNG and include a sanity-check in the normalizer to avoid scaling tiny-sample kernels.
Esther Park: Thanks Liam — added deterministic seed plumbing and a sample_count threshold in kernel_tail_normalizer to skip normalization for buckets with <64 observations (see f1b8c3e).
Priya Deshmukh: Can you add a short-run CI job that asserts the normalizer reduces variance? Also add telemetry for scaled_vs_raw_sample_ratio so we can monitor effects in prod.
Esther Park: Added nightly smoke job and telemetry counter (ci/workflows/benchmark-nightly.yml, kernel_tail_normalizer emits normalized_ratio metric).
Marco Silva: Code looks good. One nit: histogram serializer change should be backward compatible with existing dashboards. Please confirm the metadata field is optional when reading older payloads.
Esther Park: Confirmed — serializer uses presence check; dashboards default to raw when metadata absent. Added doc note in bench/reports/README.md.
